title: Peter Was Given No Hearing
english: …to be honored with the very title of bishop. But perhaps what I say may seem to your piety somewhat harsh and unbrotherly; yet in truth it is not so. For we suppose, perhaps, that we have shown the old man mercy by leaving him only the title; but it would have been far better to consider the other side as well. For he says that he could clear his good name, but that he was given no opportunity to defend himself, nor indeed was he granted a canonical hearing. Had anything of the kind taken place, the record of the proceedings would itself have made his case plain: either proving that he had been caught by the charges and declared guilty, with nothing more to say as one who had been wronged, or else declaring him free and giving him back the right to preside over the church that had been placed under his hand. But since nothing of the kind was done, he cries out against what has happened; he says that he has suffered intolerable injustice…
translator_notes: This section completes the sentence begun at the end of the previous one: 'not even…to be honored with the very title of bishop'.
τὸν πρεσβύτην is 'the old man', that is, Peter the bishop; it is not the word for a presbyter (πρεσβύτερος).
κλῆσις here is the title of bishop: 'leaving him only the title'.
συστῆναι τῇ οἰκείᾳ ὑπολήψει: 'clear his good name'.
The number 278 printed inside the Greek (μακρῷ δὲ 278 ἦν) is the PG column number, not part of the text.
The section ends mid-sentence; Peter's complaint continues in the next section with καὶ ἀθέσμως ἐκβεβλῆσθαι ('and that he has been thrown out unlawfully').
baehrens: PG 77; CPG 5378? Epistula canonica ad Domnum ep rem early

title: A Fair Trial Before the Bishops
english: …and that he has been thrown out unlawfully; and he adds that all the money belonging to him was seized as well.

Let your holiness, then, bearing in mind what the divine canons decree and what befits the church and those appointed to sacred ministry, and yielding besides to our letters, stop the old man's tears. And if he chooses to go to trial against those who bring the charges against him, let him be tried in the customary way before your piety, with the most God-fearing bishops under your authority sitting with you, of course, unless he objects to some of them as suspect. For we do not believe that any of the most God-fearing bishops harbors hostility toward a brother; but so that this may not become a pretext that undoes the judgment he will receive, by making it seem not to have been…
translator_notes: The opening words continue Peter's reported complaint from the previous section: καὶ ἀθέσμως ἐκβεβλῆσθαι, 'and that he has been thrown out unlawfully'.
στη 279 σάτω is the imperative στησάτω ('let … stop'), split in the printed text by the PG column number 279; the number is not part of the Greek.
τοῦ πρεσβύτου is 'the old man', Peter, as in the previous section.
τὰ παρ' ἡμῶν δυσωπηθεῖσα γράμματα: literally 'moved by the letters from us'; rendered 'yielding besides to our letters'.
Peter is the subject of ἕλοιτο, δικαζέσθω and παραιτοῖτο. αὐτῆς ('her') refers to 'your piety' (τῆς σῆς θεοσεβείας), so the bishops who sit with Domnus are those under his authority.
The section ends mid-sentence at πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἐν; the clause is completed at the start of the next section ('…justly done').
baehrens: PG 77; CPG 5378? Epistula canonica ad Domnum ep rem mid

title: Peter's Money Must Be Returned
english: …justly done, there is no harm in some who are under suspicion being absent from the tribunal.
2. On the bishop's having authority over everything that belongs to the church.

As for the money unjustly taken from him, it is right that it be given back, for two reasons. First, because nothing of the kind ought to have happened at all; and because it deeply grieves the most God-fearing bishops everywhere on earth, and casts them into the utmost dejection, to be required to give account of how they managed the expenses that fall to them, whether these come from the church's revenues or from the offerings of certain people. For each of us will give account of his own time to the Judge of all (Romans 14:12). For treasures and immovable estates, inalienable for the…
translator_notes: This section completes the sentence begun at the end of the previous one (δίκῃ πεποιῆσθαι δοκεῖν). The full clause reads: 'but so that this may not become a pretext that undoes the judgment he will receive, by making it seem not to have been justly done, there is no harm in some who are under suspicion being absent from the tribunal.'
οὐδὲν ἐστὶ τὸ λυποῦν: literally 'nothing is the thing that grieves'; rendered 'there is no harm'.
συνέδριον: the bench of bishops sitting in judgment; rendered 'tribunal'.

Heading 2: περὶ τοῦ πάντων τῶν ἐκκλησιαστικῶν ἔχειν τὴν ἐξουσίαν τὸν ἐπίσκοπον. τὰ ἐκκλησιαστικά ('the church's things') is rendered 'everything that belongs to the church', since the canon concerns money, revenues and estates. Like Heading 1 it is περί with an articular infinitive, so it is rendered 'On …'.
παρ' αὐτοῦ with ληφθέντα: 'taken from him' (Peter), matching his complaint above that all his money was seized.

κατὰ δύο τρόπους: 'for two reasons'. Πρῶτον μέν is followed by two ὅτι clauses and no δέ before the text breaks off; the English keeps 'First, because …; and because …' so as not to decide whether the second ὅτι clause is the second reason.
οὐδὲ ἐχρῆν ὅλως: 'nothing of the kind ought to have happened at all'.
The number 280 printed inside ἁπαν 280 ταχόσε (ἁπανταχόσε, 'everywhere') is the PG column number, not part of the text.
τῆς τινων καρποφορίας: offerings (literally 'fruit-bearing') brought by some of the faithful; rendered 'the offerings of certain people'.
τῶν ἰδίων καιρῶν: 'of his own times', that is, the period of his own charge; rendered 'his own time'.
τῷ πάντων κριτῇ refers to God and is capitalized 'the Judge of all'. Possible echo of Hebrews 12:23 (κριτῇ θεῷ πάντων); uncertain, so not cited inline.

The Greek ends at ταῖς (presumably ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις, 'to the churches'); nothing after it survives in the copy-text. The English ends with an ellipsis and does not supply the missing verb. ἀνεκποιήτως (adverb, 'inalienably') is rendered with the adjective 'inalienable' for readable English.
baehrens: PG 77; CPG 5378? Epistula canonica ad Domnum ep rem close
